heading: San Francisco
description: A map of San Francisco with toggleable layers: the five parts of the city, 41 neighborhoods and SF Find's 117, known-as names, landmarks, historic and cultural districts, supervisor, Assembly, State Senate and congressional districts, main streets, freeways, BART, Muni Metro and the cable cars, and the trains of the nine-county Bay Area.

reps.note: Names open each person’s official page. San Francisco’s Board of Supervisors elections are nonpartisan. Supervisor Districts 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 are on the November 3 ballot, and new terms start January 8. Each U.S. representative is shown for the district they were elected on; the congressional lines on the map are the new Proposition 50 ones used on November 3, and the winners take office in January. Last change {date}.

transit.title: Transit nearby
transit.none: No bus stop within ¼ mile
transit.every: about every {h} min on weekday middays
transit.note: Muni bus routes with a stop within ¼ mile, about a 5-minute walk. Numbers with a double ring come every 10 minutes or better on weekdays. Tap a number to draw the route. Muni schedules, week of {week}; Bay Wheels’ station list.

nearby.note: Straight-line distances; half a mile is about a 10-minute walk. Rec & Park, the San Francisco Public Library and the State’s school directory. Counts parks, not courts. Schools are SFUSD’s own; most places are assigned by lottery, not distance. Places of worship (OpenStreetMap) show while their layer is on. Soft-story buildings are the wood-frame apartment buildings over garages or shops the City required to be strengthened; nearly all have been.

steps.title: A city that is also a county
steps.text: San Francisco is one government, the City and County, run by a mayor and an 11-member Board of Supervisors. The colours here are a rough guide to how locals split the city: Downtown, the Northside, the West Side, Central and the Southeast.

steps.title: Neighborhoods and the names people say
steps.text: The City reports its figures by 41 Analysis Neighborhoods. The names in italics are what people actually say: SoMa, the Tenderloin, NoPa, Cow Hollow.

steps.title: Getting around
steps.text: BART and Muni Metro share the tunnel under Market Street. BART crosses the Bay to Oakland and the East Bay, Caltrain runs down the Peninsula to San José from 4th & King, and ferries leave the Ferry Building for Marin, Alameda, Oakland and Vallejo.

steps.title: Nine counties
steps.text: The Bay Area is nine counties and 101 cities and towns, from Santa Rosa to San José. The suburban lens shows the typical drive to downtown San Francisco with no traffic, town by town.

steps.title: Tap anywhere
steps.text: Tap any spot or search an address, and the card shows the neighborhood it’s in, what living there is like, the transit nearby, and its supervisor, state and congressional districts.
